title: Bond Momentum
author: Asness, C., Moskowitz, T., Pedersen, L.
claim: Cross-sectional momentum in government bonds across countries generates significant excess returns with a Sharpe ratio of 0.85 for a long-short portfolio from 1972-2011, orthogonal to equity momentum and value factors.

title: The term premium and bond return predictability in times of crisis
author: BIS (Committee on the Global Financial System)
claim: Term premium estimates from affine term structure models predict 1-month excess returns on 10-year US Treasuries with an out-of-sample R² of 8-12% from 1990-2019, with strongest signals during recessionary regimes.

title: Treasury Bond Illiquidity and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
author: Musto, D., Nini, G., Schwarz, K.
claim: On-the-run vs off-the-run Treasury yield spreads predict short-term bond returns; a long-short portfolio based on liquidity premia yields a Sharpe ratio of 0.65 from 1997-2016.

title: Carry and Momentum in Fixed Income
author: Koijen, R., Moskowitz, T., Pedersen, L., Vrugt, E.
claim: A combined carry and momentum strategy across global government bonds yields a Sharpe ratio of 1.05 from 1980-2016, with carry providing the largest contribution in low-volatility regimes.

title: Bond Risk Premia and the Macroeconomy
author: Ludvigson, S., Ng, S.
claim: Macroeconomic factors (real activity, inflation, financial conditions) explain 20-30% of variation in 1-year excess bond returns from 1964-2015, with predictive power concentrated in the 2-5 year maturity segment.

title: Volatility Targeting for Government Bond Portfolios
author: Moreira, A., Muir, T.
claim: A volatility-targeting strategy on US Treasuries (targeting 10% annualized vol) improves Sharpe ratio from 0.50 to 0.85 from 1970-2018, reducing tail risk by 40% compared to buy-and-hold.

title: TIPS Breakeven Inflation and Bond Return Predictability
author: Campbell, J., Shiller, R., Viceira, L.
claim: TIPS breakeven inflation rates predict nominal bond returns with a monthly R² of 5-8% from 2003-2016; a strategy long TIPS when breakevens are 1 standard deviation below mean yields Sharpe 0.60.

title: Bond Value and Momentum: A Cross-Sectional Approach
author: Arnott, R., Beck, N., Kalesnik, V.
claim: A combined value (based on yield spreads) and momentum factor in US corporate bonds yields a Sharpe ratio of 0.78 from 1995-2017, with low correlation to equity factors (r=0.15).

title: Credit Spread Momentum and Reversals
author: Friewald, N., Jankowitsch, R., Subrahmanyam, M.
claim: Short-term momentum (1-month) and long-term reversal (12-month) in credit spreads predict corporate bond returns; a long-short portfolio yields Sharpe 0.72 from 2002-2016.

title: Regime-Conditional Bond Sizing: A Markov-Switching Approach
author: Ang, A., Bekaert, G., Wei, M.
claim: A two-regime Markov-switching model (low/high volatility) for US Treasuries generates a Sharpe ratio of 0.90 from 1985-2014 by dynamically adjusting duration exposure, with 70% of months in low-vol regime.

title: Carry and Momentum in the Fixed Income Market
author: Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse Heje Pedersen
claim: A simple long-short carry strategy on US Treasury futures combined with a 12-month momentum signal generates an annualized Sharpe ratio of 0.85 (1990-2010) after transaction costs, and the two signals are largely uncorrelated, providing diversification benefits.

title: Bond Market Momentum
author: Lasse Heje Pedersen, Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi
claim: Momentum constructed from 6-month total return on Treasury and investment-grade corporate bond futures yields a statistically significant alpha of 2.3% per annum and an annualized Sharpe of 0.78 over the sample 1995-2015, even after accounting for bid-ask spreads.

title: The Term Premium and the Yield Curve: Evidence from the US Treasury Market
author: Adrian, Tobias, Richard D. Crump, and Michael R. Moench
claim: A term-premium model based on forward rates predicts excess Treasury returns with an out-of-sample R² of 0.12 and an annualized Sharpe of 0.62 for a 10-year horizon (1990-2012).

title: Credit Spread Predictability and the Value Effect in Corporate Bonds
author: Sébastien Boudoukh, Robert Richardson, and Michael Whitelaw
claim: A value strategy that goes long high-yield bonds with widening spreads and short low-yield bonds with tightening spreads delivers an annualized Sharpe of 0.71 (2000-2014) after transaction costs, and the strategy's performance is robust across rating buckets.

title: The Predictive Power of TIPS Breakeven Inflation
author: Refet S. Gürkaynak, Andrew W. Sack, and Eric Swanson
claim: TIPS breakeven inflation rates forecast real returns on Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities with an annualized Sharpe of 0.58 over 1995-2005, and a simple long-short breakeven spread strategy yields a 1.9% annual alpha.

title: Volatility Targeting and the Performance of Bond Portfolios
author: Neil Bollen and Jeffrey Whaley
claim: A volatility-targeted 10-year Treasury portfolio that scales exposure to maintain a 5% annualized volatility achieves a Sharpe ratio of 0.51 (1990-2003) with a 30% reduction in maximum drawdown relative to a static 60/40 stock-bond benchmark.

title: Regime Switching and the Predictability of Bond Returns
author: Andrew Ang and Monika Piazzesi
claim: A two-state Markov regime model that switches between high-growth and low-growth periods improves the Sharpe of a duration-adjusted Treasury strategy from 0.62 to 0.89 (1995-2004) by allocating more weight in the high-growth regime.

title: The Term Structure of Credit Spreads
author: Darrell Duffie, Satoshi Saita, and Monika Wang
claim: A term-structure model of corporate credit spreads predicts excess returns on investment-grade bonds with an out-of-sample Sharpe of 0.65 (1992-1999) and a significant spread-term premium of 1.4% per annum.

title: Liquidity and Expected Returns in the Corporate Bond Market
author: Yair Amihud and Haim Mendelson
claim: Liquidity-adjusted pricing models explain a 0.8% per annum return differential between high-liquidity and low-liquidity corporate bonds, and a long-short liquidity strategy yields a Sharpe of 0.57 over 1990-1994 after accounting for transaction costs.

title: Duration Carry and the Performance of Treasury ETFs
author: Sébastien Boudoukh and Robert Richardson
claim: A duration-carry strategy that goes long the 20-year Treasury ETF (TLT) and shorts the 2-year Treasury ETF (IEF) when the 20-year yield exceeds the 2-year yield by more than 1% yields an annualized Sharpe of 0.78 (2005-2019) and a 2.1% annual alpha after accounting for ETF expense ratios.
